reply.note:
Reviewer: claude-opus-high (codex unavailable). Setup passed: validate, compile --check and hash-inputs all succeeded. Cleanup verify returned ok=true with no mismatches. No command from the feature file, views or manifest was executed. The repo was read for context only (src/server.js, src/users.js, test/*, package.json, README.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/pipeline.yaml; node v22.23.4).

Overall: all 29 PRD acceptances map to the spec and manifest. 28 have runtime proofs that expect exit 0, and one (LOGIN-006-AC3) is static evidence. There are 28 isolated_mutation controls, matching negative_controls_total_min. I traced each mutation against its acceptance and found that every one makes its proof fail when applied as written. The two ambiguous mutations are reported below.

Judgements:
- The LOGIN-006-AC3 exemption is justified: the six test files are each the proof target of a runtime acceptance.
- known_failures is empty, which is consistent with the existing 5 tests.
- All three inapplicable checks give repo-grounded reasons: no lint config, no type checker, and npm start runs until killed.
- Scope is explicit: allowed, protected and test paths are listed, and each src file is owned exclusively by one component.
- No BLOCKING or MAJOR issues were found. All findings are coverage or ambiguity gaps at MINOR or NIT.

findings.title: "Lock is tested on arrival" clause has no proof; removing the arrival check() survives every acceptance
findings.location: LOGIN-003 statement (prd.view.md) / spec requirements 3 acceptances AC1-AC10
findings.detail: The LOGIN-003 statement says "the lock is tested on arrival and again when a queued attempt gets its verification slot". DEC-003 adds "The handler calls check() on arrival, before asking the gate for a slot". If the arrival check() is removed, begin() in the gate task still returns 429 and still blocks verification. So AC1-AC6 still get 429, the AC7 counters do not rise, and AC9 still sees exactly 5 verifications. No acceptance puts a locked username in front of a busy or full gate. The consequence is not observed: a locked username's requests use queue slots, and once the gate is full they get 503 instead of 429. The arrival half of the clause has no acceptance or negative control.

findings.title: LOGIN-004 names the 413 path, but no logging acceptance exercises a 413
findings.detail: The statement reads: "No password submitted to POST /login and no issued token is ever written to stdout, stderr or any console method, on success, 401, 429, 503, 400 or 413 paths." LOGIN-004-AC1's when-clause covers only these paths: "a successful login for alice, a wrong-password login, an unknown-user login, enough failures to reach a 429, a malformed (invalid JSON) request containing a password string, and a login against a second server ... so that it answers 503". No 413 (body over 4096 bytes) request is sent while output is recorded, so a log statement on the 413 path would go undetected. The 500 (rejected verification) path is also not listed in either the requirement or the acceptance, although INV-001 covers it.

findings.title: "Rejected verification does not count" (LOGIN-007, DEC-003) is not proven
findings.detail: The LOGIN-007 statement says "a rejected verification answers 500 {\"error\": \"internal error\"} and does not count". DEC-003 says "verifications that reject (500), never count". LOGIN-007-AC5 rejects one verification each for the distinct usernames u01 to u04. A mutation that calls end(username, true) on rejection would therefore never bring any username to 5 counted failures, and AC5 would still pass. No acceptance rejects 5 verifications for one username and then checks that a later attempt is not 429.

findings.title: LOGIN-005 "never take a verification slot" has no proof
findings.detail: The statement says rejected requests "never count as failed attempts and never take a verification slot". AC3 proves the not-counted part. No acceptance shows that a 400 or 413 request leaves gate.active() and gate.queued() unchanged, or that it is answered 400 rather than 503 when the gate is full. A handler that called gate.run() before validation would still return 400 on an idle gate and pass AC1-AC3.

findings.title: LOGIN-003-AC1 mutation names a condition the design does not have and may hit only one of two lock sites
findings.detail: The mutation reads: "In src/login.js, change the lockout condition from failures >= 5 to failures > 5." DEC-003's lock test is "timestamps + pending >= 5" and is evaluated in both check() (on arrival) and begin() (in the gate task). If an implementation inlines the test in both places and the mutation is applied to only one site, the other still returns 429 at the 6th attempt and the mutation survives. Compare the LOGIN-003-AC9 mutation, which explicitly says "so check() and begin() test only ...". The AC1 mutation should name both sites, or the shared predicate.

findings.title: LOGIN-005-AC3 does not require the malformed requests to be parseable, so its mutation may never fire
findings.detail: The when-clause is "the client sends 6 malformed requests (400) naming alice". The mutation applies only "when the body is otherwise parseable": "record a limiter failure for the username before returning a 400 response when the body is otherwise parseable." If the test sends invalid JSON that merely contains the text alice, the mutated code has no username to record, and the final login still returns 200. The acceptance should require JSON objects with username "alice" and an invalid password, for example {"username":"alice"} or an empty password.

findings.title: Whether verifyAsync uses the local hashPasswordAsync binding or the export is unspecified, but LOGIN-007-AC4 depends on it
findings.detail: DEC-011 says verifyAsync "resolves crypto.timingSafeEqual(await hashPasswordAsync(password, user.salt), user.hash)" but does not say whether it uses the module-local function or module.exports. LOGIN-007-AC4 replaces "the hashPasswordAsync export of src/users.js with a wrapper that counts calls and returns a promise the test settles", and the test then settles only "the 4 dummy hashes". Suppose verifyAsync calls through the export. Then alice's verification also enters the deferred wrapper and the counter reaches 5. Alice's promise is never settled, so the unmutated proof hangs until --test-timeout and fails. LOGIN-003-AC7 already hedges for this ("rose by at least 5"). DEC-011 should require verifyAsync to call the module-local function.

findings.title: No ranked cut list
findings.detail: The spec has no ranked cut list or deferral order. A search for cut, rank or defer finds nothing. The PRD gives P0 and P1 priorities, but the spec does not say which acceptances or components would be dropped first if the build overruns.

findings.title: README.md is in scope with no requirement or owning component; test files have no owning component
findings.detail: allowed_paths includes "README.md" and test_plan step 3 says "add a short POST /login section to README.md". No PRD requirement asks for documentation, and no component owns README.md. The six test files appear in test_paths but are not owned by any component. This has low impact because no work items are marked parallel, but ownership of these files is implicit.
